reason: I'll build the receiving parts first: the arrows show branches carrying messages toward the cell body.
expectation: I expect the branches to attach to the nerve-cell bodies and complete that goal.

alternatives.reason: The channels also have a clear job in the fibres, but I want to start with where messages are received.

effect: The receiving branches are attached; the long fibres still need to be added and fitted with channels.
reaction: The attached branches make the receiving side clearer.
reason: I'll fit the channels to the fibres, as the goal asks. The picture shows ions passing through their open gates.
expectation: I expect channel-bearing fibres that can later connect to the nerve cells.

alternatives.reason: I could attach the fibres first, but fitting their channels addresses the current goal directly.

effect: The picture shows how local ion movements pass an electrical change along the fibre; the next goal is to join it to the cell bodies.
reaction: I was surprised that no single ion travels the whole length.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it connects the receiving parts to the message-carrying fibres.
expectation: I expect complete nerve cells with receiving branches and channel-bearing long fibres.

effect: The branches and fibres now form continuous nerve cells, and the picture shows chemical messengers crossing to the next cell. The remaining goal is to add blood vessels.
reaction: The switch from an electrical change to chemical messengers at the ending is interesting.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and the vessels can bring oxygen and food to the nerve cells.
expectation: I expect fine blood vessels to lie alongside the nerve cells and supply them with oxygen and food.

effect: The vessels completed the nervous tissue, showing that the cells carrying messages also need food and oxygen.
reaction: That connection to the cells’ basic needs made sense, though the final pairing was predictable.

mostWorthwhile.text: Fitting channels to the fibres was most worthwhile: the sequence explained how an electrical change travels without one ion going the whole way.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the blood vessels was the least engaging because it was the only combination offered and its purpose was already clear.

surprise.text: I was surprised that neighbouring channels open in turn rather than one ion travelling the fibre’s whole length.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary; even the only-option steps had clear purposes.

continue.text: I would continue another chapter to see how nerve messages connect to other body functions. The electrical-to-chemical handoff made me curious.
